FXUS65 KPSR 060806
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
105 AM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Major waterways such as the Salt and Gila rivers will continue to 
experience high volume flows through at least the weekend due to dam 
releases.

- With the exception of a slight chance for showers and 
thunderstorms over parts of south-central Arizona today, dry weather 
will be common through at least the middle of next week. 

- Temperatures will warm very near daily normals through the middle 
of next week. 
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Sunday/...
Early morning objective analysis depicts a more progressive flow 
pattern across the Conus with elongated troughing over the Great 
Lakes/Ohio River valley, as well as extending from the northern 
Rockies into the lower Colorado River valley. In fact, WV imagery 
highlights a very distinct vorticity center descending into southern 
Nevada which will become a major player in the local forecast over 
the next 24 hours. Trends in both global and high resolution 
modeling point towards more rapid deepening and forced ascent as 
this feature propagates into south-central Arizona by this 
afternoon. Recent sfc dewpoints suggest higher low level moisture 
content than models have previously forecast, and with diurnal 
mixing and upslope flow, mixing ratios 6-7 g/kg ascending and 
saturating near the H7 layer seems attainable. As the vorticity 
center intensifies and becomes a closed circulation, synoptic ascent 
will also increase further supporting the formation of scattered 
showers from Phoenix north and east. While midlevel lapse rates are 
not particularly steep, the introduction of modest cooling aloft and 
moisture intrusion at the top of the boundary layer may tap 100 J/kg 
MLCape leading to a few isolated thunderstorms. Most recent 
initialized NBM POPs were higher than previous iterations, however 
have raised and expanded these values somewhat based on the various 
HRRR and REFS trends. 

In the immediate wake of this vorticty center and on the western 
periphery of the closed circulation, higher momentum northerly winds 
will surge down the lower Colorado River valley this afternoon 
through Saturday morning. Winds speeds within the H9-H8 mixing depth 
do not appear any stronger than 20-30kt, and high resolution models 
forecast gusts over 30 mph only across ridge tops and 20-30 mph at 
lower elevation population centers resulting in minimal impacts. As 
the cutoff vorticity center travels into northern Mexico over the 
weekend, sharp ridging over the Great Basin will force strong 
subsidence and sfc pressure rises. This classic cold season pattern 
will shift enhanced nocturnal/morning easterly winds into south-
central Arizona further drying the environment above the H9 layer 
with total column PWATs falling well below 0.50". Otherwise, notable 
H5 height rises behind the exiting wave with readings 582-585dm will 
support temperatures warming back very near daily normals. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Monday through Thursday/... 
With northern stream jet energy retreating towards the Canadian 
border under broad ridging, several weak low amplitude features will 
align in the southern stream over northern Mexico during the first 
half of the week before large scale hemispheric pattern 
amplification becomes a dominating feature. Predominant anti-
cyclonic flow will continue to promote surface pressure rises over 
the intermountain West and dry N/NE boundary layer flow. The vast 
majority of ensemble membership keeps any notable shortwave ascent 
removed from the CWA, and confidence is very good that dry 
conditions will prevail through at least the middle of the week. 
With H5 heights remaining nearly constant in a 580-584dm range, 
forecast numerical spread is rather narrow indicating very good 
confidence in a persistence type forecast and readings very near 
climatology. Ensemble spread grows markedly towards the end of next 
week as pronounced northern stream pattern amplification driven 
largely by an unusual early season sudden stratospheric warming 
(SSW) event unfolds. The perturbation of the polar vortex should 
cause poleward ridge retrogression while deep negative height 
anomalies descend equatorward into the NE Conus and Pacific NW. 
While operational models are consistent in focusing strong jet 
energy and Pacific moisture towards northern California with 
inconsequential shortwave energy into the Southwest, there is a non-
trivial amount of NAEFS members suggesting much deeper, intense 
troughing moving into the local area next weekend. Given this 
amplification phase, continued wide ensemble spread and potentially 
large variations in operational models yielding low forecast 
confidence should be expected into next week. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0555Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Winds will tend to follow their typical diurnal tendencies with 
speeds aob 7 kt through the period. Extended periods of light and 
variable winds are expected, especially around diurnal transitions. 
Winds will reestablish an easterly component overnight tonight. 
Winds tomorrow afternoon/evening will likely exhibit more of a NW 
component. FEW-SCT clouds will be common through the period. Some 
FEW clouds with decks aoa 6-7 kt are expected to develop tomorrow 
afternoon/evening, mainly north and east of Phoenix. Will also have 
to watch for isolated showers tomorrow evening, but better chances 
for showers are in the higher terrain to the north and east of 
Phoenix.


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No major aviation weather concerns are expected through the next 24 
hours under mostly clear skies. Winds will be light through mid 
morning with speeds aob 7 kt, periods of light and variable to calm 
winds are also possible. By late tomorrow morning wind speeds will 
pick up and be around 10-15 kt, with some gusts up around 20 kt 
expected during the afternoon and evening. Wind directions will be 
out of the west at KIPL prior to going N/NW late tomorrow morning. 
Winds will continue to exhibit a northerly component at KBLH. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A few isolated showers or thunderstorms may impact higher terrain 
areas north and east of Phoenix today, however wetting rainfall 
chances are minimal. Otherwise, dry conditions will prevail across 
the region through at least the middle of next week. Minimum 
afternoon humidity levels will largely fall into a 20-30% range in 
western districts and 30-50% in eastern districts. This will follow 
fair to good overnight recovery in western districts and good to 
excellent levels in eastern districts. Northerly winds gusts 20-30 
mph will be common in western districts this afternoon through 
Saturday, while a period of enhanced morning easterly winds will 
develop over Arizona early next week. Outside of these time frames, 
wind speeds will be light with limited gustiness. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...18
LONG TERM...18 
AVIATION...Berislavich
FIRE WEATHER...18
